extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers seeking independent fellowships (early-career researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Information and eligibility/requirements for applying to the Branco Weiss Fellowship (Society in Science), a postdoctoral fellowship supporting original, independent research between the PhD and a first faculty appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to support postdoctoral researchers after their PhD and before their first faculty appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be at the postdoctoral stage (i.e., have completed a PhD and not yet hold a faculty appointment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — disciplinary scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship is open for postdocs from all around the world and from all disciplines (natural and social sciences, humanities and engineering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers in any discipline are eligible; the program explicitly lists natural and social sciences, humanities, and engineering as included fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research idea — originality and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must propose original and independent research ideas that fall outside the scope of large-scale research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship favors research that is novel, investigator-driven, and not part of large collaborative/consortium projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution — applicant choice and mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows can choose the best possible academic institution, anywhere in the world, to perform their research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no institutional restriction — recipients are free to select any academic host institution globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows will receive support for up to five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award can fund the fellow's research for a period up to five years (maximum duration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funds — flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows decide for themselves how the financial resources will be allocated — for their own salary, for staff, for equipment or for a combination of these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship provides flexible budgeting to cover salary, personnel, equipment, or combinations tailored to the project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of awards per year
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim is to award up to ten fellowships per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual target number of fellowships is up to ten; actual number may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadline and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for applications is 15 January each year at 17:00 Swiss local time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be submitted by the stated annual deadline (15 January, 17:00 Swiss local time). Detailed application process and timing information available on the external Branco Weiss Fellowship website.
